Four-Cycle Engine Theory Section 3: Four-Cycle Engine Theory Introduction Four events must occur in the correct sequence and at the correct time for the engine to run correctly. These events are (A) intake, (B) compression, (C) power, and (D) exhaust. (A) Intake (C) Power 001684 The piston is traveling from top dead center (TDC) to bottom dead center (BDC). The cam has opened the intake valve. The piston's downward movement in the cylinder creates a partial vacuum in the cylinder. Air at atmospheric pressure is drawn into the cylinder through the airbox and is mixed with fuel, supplied by the mixer, as it enters the cylinder. The intake stroke is complete when the piston reaches BDC. (B) Compression 001686 Combustion is already in progress when the piston reaches TDC. The intake and exhaust valves remain closed as expanding gases of combustion force the piston downward. (D) Exhaust 001687 The exhaust stroke begins when the piston has reached BDC and has started its upward movement. The intake valve is closed, and the exhaust valve is open to let gases escape. 001685 As the piston reaches BDC, both the intake and exhaust valves are closed. The piston moves upward toward TDC and the fuel-air mixture is compressed. Ignition occurs just before the piston reaches TDC. 459cc Engine Service Manual 13

Maintaining Air Cleaner WARNING Risk of fire. Never operate engine without the air cleaner installed. Operating engine without the air cleaner could result in death or serious injury. (W000249) A correctly serviced air cleaner protects internal engine parts from dirt and dust particles in the air. If air cleaner instructions are not carefully followed, dirt and dust normally collected in the air cleaner will be drawn into the engine. Particulates will wear on cylinder bores and piston rings, allowing particles to enter the crankcase and contaminate the oil, forming an abrasive mixture which will quickly wear internal moving parts. Inspect the air cleaner on every engine serviced or repaired. If the air cleaner shows signs of neglect, show it to the user before cleaning. Instruct the user on correct care techniques to assure long engine life. NOTE: Replace worn or damaged air cleaner gaskets and mounting gaskets to prevent dirt and dust from entering the engine due to incorrect sealing. Replace bent air cleaner mounting bracket if necessary. Troubleshooting Most complaints concerning engine operation can be classified as one or a combination of the following: • Will not start • Hard starting • Lack of power • Runs rough • Vibration • Overheating • Noise • High oil consumption NOTE: What appears to be an engine malfunction may be a fault of the equipment connected to the engine rather than the engine. If equipment is suspect, see equipment affecting engine operation. Systematic Inspection If engine will not start and the cause of malfunction is not readily apparent, perform a systematic inspection in the following order: 1. Fuel 2. Ignition 3. Compression This inspection, performed in a systematic manner, can usually be done in a matter of minutes. It is the quickest 459cc Engine Service Manual General Information and surest method of determining the cause of failure. The basic inspection procedure is the same for all engine models. Cylinder Leakdown Test Testing Procedure WARNING Moving Parts. Keep clothing, hair, and appendages away from moving parts. Failure to do so could result in death or serious injury. (W000111) Proceed as follows to perform a cylinder leakdown test: 1. Disconnect the ECM. 2. Manually open the throttle plate on the ETC. 3. Connect a remote button starter switch from the battery positive (+) to the starter relay. 4. Align piston at TDC. 5. Install cylinder leakdown tester in the spark plug hole. 6. Pressurize cylinder to 90 psi (621 kPa). 7. Observe cylinder leakage and identify location of air leak. NOTE: If leaking into intake or exhaust port, inspect valve face and valve seat condition. Cylinder Head and Valves Figure 9-4. Figure 9-4. Check Valve Springs 004442 Gasket Removal Verify sealing surface is completely clean and free of old gasket material before installing a new gasket. Residual gasket material or dirt can prevent the new gasket from sealing completely. An incorrectly sealed gasket may cause the engine to leak oil, lose compression, or overheat. It is critical to completely remove old gasket material without damaging sealing surfaces. Aluminum is very soft and easy to scratch and gouge. A new gasket may not seal completely if the underlying surface is damaged. Generac does not recommend using a wire brush or abrasive sanding to remove gaskets. Use a metal gasket scraper specifically designed for this purpose. Scrape gasket at a shallow angle—almost parallel to the sealing surface. Wipe sealing surface with a clean, dry, lint-free rag after removing gasket residue. If the gasket is difficult to scrape off, spray it with an aerosol gasket removal compound. Allow the compound to soak into the gasket for the length of time recommended by the manufacturer (typically 10– 20 minutes), then use the gasket scraper again. NOTE: Some gasket removal compounds contain chemicals damaging to plastics. Read and follow the directions on the product label before use. Section 10: Electric Starter Electric Starter General Information See Figure 10-1. The starter motor utilizes a solenoid, similar to an automobile starter, to assist in pinion gear engagement. When the starter motor is activated, the pinion gear engages a ring gear attached to the engine flywheel and cranks the engine. Figure 10-1. Figure 10-1. Starter Motor 021329 Troubleshooting IMPORTANT NOTE: Do not rotate engine with electric starter while spark plugs are removed, unless using a compression gauge. Arcing at the spark plug ends may ignite fuel vapor exiting the spark plug hole. NOTE: If a starting problem is encountered, inspect the engine thoroughly to eliminate it as the cause of starting difficulty. Check engine for free rotation by removing spark plugs and flywheel guard and turning the crankshaft with a socket and ratchet or breaker bar. Verify it rotates freely. Starter Troubleshooting Engine will not crank if: • Faulty safety interlocks. • Discharged battery. • Faulty electrical connections. • Faulty starter motor switch (open circuit). • Open circuit in starter motor. • Brushes sticking, etc. • Faulty solenoid. Starter motor spins but does not crank engine: • Sticking pinion gear due to dirt. • Damaged pinion or ring gear. • Damaged or faulty battery. • Incorrect rotation due to reversed motor polarity. • All motors rotate counterclockwise viewed from pinion gear. • Damaged solenoid. Starter motor spins but will not stop: • Faulty starter switch. • Solenoid stuck engaged. Test Equipment Digital Multimeter (DMM) See Figure 10-2. Section 11: Lubrication System Lubrication System Figure 11-1. Description The Generac 459 CC G26 G-Force Single engine uses a full pressure lubrication system with an oil filter. A gerotor oil pump draws oil from a screened oil pickup in the sump and pumps oil through the oil filter. Filtered oil flows through an oil gallery in the sump and is distributed to the main bearings, connecting rod bearings, hydraulic lash adjusters, and camshaft bearings. Engine oil pressure varies with oil viscosity, ambient air temperature differences, operating temperatures, and engine load. B • Oil pressure - @ 70 °F (21 °C): 15 – 50 psi (103 – 345 kPa) Protection Systems A Remove D Low Oil Pressure Switch See Figure 11-1. The engine is usually equipped with a normally open type, low oil pressure switch (A) which closes the circuit between the terminals when oil pressure drops below 5 +/- 2 psi (34 kPA). The engine will shut down on low oil pressure if one terminal is connected to the ignition ground wire and the other terminal is connected to ground. The low oil pressure switch can also be connected to an alarm or light to indicate low oil pressure, instead of shutting down the engine. C 00049619 Figure 11-1. Low Oil Pressure Switch, Oil Fill, Oil Drain Plug, and Oil Filter A delay built into the shutdown system on some engine applications allows oil pressure to build during starting. The delay allows the engine to run for about 10 seconds before sensing oil pressure. The engine shuts down if the engine is wired for low oil pressure shutdown and the system senses low oil pressure during operation. The engine will not run until 8 psi (55 kPa) of oil pressure is reached. If a restart is attempted within five seconds after shutdown, the engine may NOT start. The system needs 10 seconds to reset. (C000135) Oil capacity of the 459 CC G26 G-Force Single engine is approximately 1.4 qt (1.3 L). See Specifications for the recommended amount for each model.
